scenario: A retailer wants to move from buying servers every few years to paying monthly for what it uses. Which cloud benefit is this?

options.text: Shifting capital expenses to operational expenses
Guaranteed zero downtime for every app
Eliminating all security responsibilities for the business

explanation: Pay-as-you-go turns large upfront CapEx into ongoing OpEx.

scenario: Which describes digital transformation?

options.text: Using technology to change how a business operates and delivers value
Moving every file to a USB drive
Upgrading every employee's laptop and network equipment to the latest models

explanation: Cloud enables new products, faster experiments and data-driven decisions.

scenario: Which cloud model runs on infrastructure shared by many customers and managed by a provider?
explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private cloud with public cloud.

scenario: A company uses Google Cloud and another cloud provider for different workloads. What is this called?
explanation: Multicloud can avoid lock-in and use each provider's strengths.

scenario: Which describes the shared responsibility model in the cloud?

options.text: The provider secures the infrastructure; customers secure their data and access
The provider is responsible for everything, including customer data access and user accounts
Responsibility is the same for every service

explanation: With SaaS the provider handles more; with IaaS the customer handles more.

scenario: Which cloud service model gives the customer the most control over operating systems?
explanation: Compute Engine is Google Cloud's IaaS for virtual machines.

scenario: What's a Google Cloud region?

options.text: A geographic area containing multiple zones
A billing account shared by several teams
A virtual network spanning several projects

explanation: Deploying across zones and regions improves availability.

scenario: Which Google Cloud network feature carries traffic over Google's private fiber between regions?

options.note: Not by default for Premium Tier.

options.text: Customer-owned leased lines to each region

explanation: Premium Tier networking keeps traffic on Google's network as long as possible.

scenario: What's the main advantage of a cloud provider's economies of scale for customers?

options.text: Lower costs per unit of computing
No need for any IT staff
Guaranteed lowest price on every product

explanation: Large providers buy and operate at lower cost per unit.

scenario: Which term describes resources that grow or shrink automatically with demand?
explanation: Autoscaling managed instance groups and serverless services scale automatically.

scenario: What is total cost of ownership (TCO)?

options.text: All costs over time, including hardware, staff and power
Only the purchase price of servers
The cost of software licenses and support contracts only

explanation: TCO comparisons help build a business case for cloud.

scenario: Which describes open source as part of Google Cloud's approach?

options.text: Support for open technologies like Kubernetes to reduce lock-in
Customers must publish all of their own application code
Open source is banned in production

explanation: Google created Kubernetes and TensorFlow and supports many open standards.

scenario: Which describes Google Cloud's sustainability goal?

options.text: Run on carbon-free energy every hour by 2030
Charge customers extra for using low-carbon regions

explanation: Region pickers show low-carbon options.

scenario: A bank wants data to stay in one country to satisfy regulators. Which concept is this?
explanation: Choose regions and use organization policies to restrict resource locations.

scenario: Which describes cloud-native application design?

options.text: Building apps from loosely coupled services that scale independently
Running one large app on a single server
options.note: That's a monolith on one host.

options.text: Avoiding automation so every change is reviewed by hand
Storing all data on local disks

explanation: Containers, microservices and managed services are common cloud-native building blocks.

scenario: Which Google Cloud resource level groups projects by department, like Finance or Engineering?
explanation: Hierarchy: organization > folders > projects > resources.

scenario: Which Google Cloud service is a serverless data warehouse for analyzing large datasets with SQL?
explanation: BigQuery separates storage and compute and bills by data processed or reserved capacity.

scenario: Which service stores unstructured data like images and backups as objects?
explanation: Storage classes: Standard, Nearline, Coldline and Archive.

scenario: Which Cloud Storage feature automatically moves objects to cheaper classes based on access patterns?
explanation: Autoclass removes the need to write lifecycle rules for class changes.

scenario: Which Cloud Storage class is cheapest for data accessed less than once a year?
explanation: Colder classes have lower storage costs but retrieval fees.

scenario: Which managed database is PostgreSQL-compatible and built for demanding transactional and analytical workloads?
explanation: Cloud SQL also offers managed PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server.

scenario: Which database offers global scale with strong consistency for relational data?
explanation: Spanner suits global financial and inventory systems.

scenario: Which service is a NoSQL document database often used for mobile and web apps?
explanation: Firestore supports real-time sync and offline mode.

scenario: Which service handles very high-throughput, low-latency NoSQL workloads like IoT time series?
explanation: Bigtable is used for analytics and operational workloads at petabyte scale.

scenario: Which service ingests streaming messages from many sources for real-time processing?
explanation: Pub/Sub decouples producers and consumers.

scenario: Which service runs Apache Beam pipelines for batch and streaming data processing?
explanation: Dataflow is fully managed and autoscaling.

scenario: Which service runs Apache Spark workloads, formerly known as Dataproc?
explanation: Google renamed Dataproc in April 2026; it supports clusters and serverless Spark.

scenario: Which tool lets business users build interactive dashboards and reports from BigQuery data?
explanation: Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio) is a free self-service reporting tool.

scenario: What's the difference between a data lake and a data warehouse?

options.text: A lake stores raw data in any format; a warehouse stores structured, modeled data
They are always the same system with two names
A lake requires a fixed schema and modeling before any data is loaded

explanation: Lakehouses combine both approaches with open table formats.

scenario: Which service catalogs and governs data across lakes and warehouses, formerly called Dataplex?
explanation: Data governance includes discovery, quality, lineage and access policies.

scenario: What is a benefit of storing business data in a single analytics platform like BigQuery?

options.text: Teams can combine data sources for better insights
Data no longer needs any security
It removes the need for backups of all source systems

explanation: Breaking down data silos supports better decisions.

scenario: Which service lets a company query data in BigQuery that lives in other clouds?
explanation: Omni runs analytics close to data in AWS or Azure.

scenario: What is Google Cloud's unified platform for building, deploying and managing AI agents and models, formerly Vertex AI?
explanation: Google renamed Vertex AI to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

scenario: Which Google product gives employees an AI assistant that searches company data and runs agents?
explanation: Gemini Enterprise was formerly called Agentspace.

scenario: Which describes generative AI?

options.text: AI that creates new content like text and images
AI that only sorts data into two categories
A database designed for storing prompts and responses
A rule-based script with fixed answers

explanation: Foundation models are trained on broad data and adapted to many tasks.

scenario: Which describes an AI agent?

options.text: A system that reasons, plans and takes actions toward a goal using tools
A static dashboard that refreshes once a month
A virtual machine image with AI libraries installed

explanation: Agents can call APIs, search data and work with other agents.

scenario: A company wants to use a model without managing infrastructure. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Use a pre-trained model through a managed API
Build a data center for GPUs
Train a model from scratch on laptops
Write and maintain rules for every possible case manually

explanation: Model Garden offers Google, partner and open models.

scenario: Which Google Cloud offering provides optimized hardware and software for training and serving large AI models?

options.note: Hardware access, not the integrated offering.

explanation: It combines TPUs, GPUs, networking and software frameworks.

scenario: Which is a responsible AI practice?

options.text: Testing models for bias and explaining their outputs
Using any available data regardless of user consent
Skipping human review for high-stakes uses

explanation: Google's AI Principles guide fairness, safety, privacy and accountability.

scenario: Which technique grounds a model's answers in a company's own documents?

options.text: Removing the system prompt to save tokens

explanation: Grounding reduces hallucinations and adds citations.

scenario: What is a hallucination in generative AI?

options.text: A confident answer that's false or unsupported
An authentication error caused by a bad API key

explanation: Grounding, human review and evaluation help reduce hallucinations.

scenario: Which Google Cloud tool lets non-developers build agents with a visual interface?
explanation: Agent Studio was formerly part of Vertex AI Studio and Agent Builder.

scenario: Which is a common business use of AI in customer service?

options.text: Virtual agents that answer common questions 24/7

explanation: Customer Engagement Suite provides conversational AI for contact centers.

scenario: Why is data quality important for machine learning?

options.text: Poor data leads to inaccurate predictions
Quality only matters for storage costs
More data always fixes bad or biased data

explanation: Garbage in, garbage out.

scenario: Which describes the difference between AI and machine learning?

options.text: ML is a subset of AI where systems learn from data
AI is a subset of ML
ML only works with images and video

explanation: Deep learning is a subset of ML using neural networks.

scenario: Which Google AI model family powers many Google Cloud generative AI features?
explanation: Gemini models are multimodal: text, images, audio, video and code.

scenario: Which BigQuery capability lets analysts create and run ML models with SQL?
explanation: BigQuery can also call Gemini models from SQL.

scenario: A company wants AI help writing code and managing Google Cloud resources. Which tool fits?

options.text: Gemini Code Assist and Gemini Cloud Assist

explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist helps design, operate and troubleshoot cloud environments.

scenario: Which Google Cloud service provides virtual machines?
explanation: Compute Engine is IaaS; Spot VMs offer large discounts for interruptible work.

scenario: Which service runs containers serverlessly and scales to zero when idle?
explanation: Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions) run event-driven code.

scenario: Which service is Google's managed Kubernetes for running containerized apps at scale?
explanation: GKE Autopilot manages nodes for you.

scenario: Which modernization approach moves VMs to the cloud with few or no changes?
explanation: Migration Center helps discover and plan migrations.

scenario: Why might a company containerize an application?

options.text: To run it consistently across environments
To make it require a specific laptop
To prevent the app from scaling unexpectedly

explanation: Containers package code with dependencies.

scenario: Which service manages APIs, including security, analytics and rate limiting?
explanation: APIs let companies expose data and services to partners securely.

scenario: Which serverless option is best for running a small piece of code when a file is uploaded?
explanation: Functions are triggered by events from Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub and more.

scenario: Which service runs VMware workloads natively on Google Cloud?

options.note: Dedicated servers for specialized workloads like Oracle.

explanation: It speeds migration of existing VMware environments.

scenario: Which approach makes it easier to release small app changes frequently?

options.text: Avoiding version control to reduce overhead

explanation: Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy support CI/CD.

scenario: Which Google Cloud service stores container images and language packages?
explanation: Artifact Registry replaced Container Registry.

scenario: A company has steady workloads that run 24/7 for three years. Which pricing option saves the most on VMs?
explanation: Sustained use discounts apply automatically to some VM types.

scenario: Which Google Cloud service gives dedicated, low-latency private connectivity from a data center?
explanation: Dedicated and Partner Interconnect options exist.

scenario: Which service caches website content at Google's edge locations to speed delivery?
explanation: Cloud CDN works with Google Cloud load balancers.

scenario: Which Workspace-based approach helps employees collaborate in real time on documents?

options.text: Google Workspace apps like Docs and Drive
Compute Engine VMs for each employee

explanation: Collaboration tools are part of many digital transformation efforts.

scenario: Which tool helps assess on-premises servers and estimate cloud costs before migration?
explanation: It provides discovery, TCO estimates and migration planning.

scenario: Which Google Cloud service controls who can do what on which resources?

options.note: Restricts configurations, not who can act.

explanation: Grant roles to principals following least privilege.

scenario: Which security model assumes no user or device is trusted by default, even on the internal network?
explanation: Google's BeyondCorp model inspired Chrome Enterprise Premium.

scenario: Which service protects web apps from DDoS attacks and common exploits?
explanation: Cloud Armor works with external Application Load Balancers.

scenario: Which product gives a centralized view of security risks and misconfigurations in Google Cloud?
explanation: It detects threats, vulnerabilities and posture issues.

scenario: Which Google product is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR platform for security teams?
explanation: Google Security Operations was formerly called Chronicle.

scenario: Which product provides threat intelligence from Mandiant and VirusTotal?
explanation: Threat intelligence helps defenders understand attackers.

scenario: By default, how does Google Cloud protect customer data stored at rest?
explanation: Customers can use their own keys with Cloud KMS (CMEK).

scenario: Which service lets customers manage their own encryption keys?
explanation: Cloud HSM and External Key Manager provide more control.

scenario: Which service discovers and protects sensitive data like credit card numbers?
explanation: It can classify, mask and de-identify data.

scenario: Which tool lets administrators restrict where resources can be created, such as only in EU regions?

options.note: Limits data movement, not resource locations.

explanation: Organization policies apply constraints across the hierarchy.

scenario: Which feature creates a security perimeter around Google Cloud services to reduce data exfiltration?
explanation: Perimeters block data from leaving protected projects.

scenario: Where can customers find Google Cloud's compliance certifications like ISO 27001?
explanation: Google Cloud supports many frameworks such as SOC 2, PCI DSS and HIPAA.

scenario: Which principle should guide IAM role assignment?
explanation: Prefer predefined or custom roles over basic roles.

scenario: Which feature requires users to prove identity with more than a password?
explanation: Security keys and passkeys are phishing-resistant.

scenario: Which describes Google Cloud's approach to customer data privacy?

options.text: Customers own their data and Google doesn't use it for ads
All customer data is public by default
Google may use it for ads freely

explanation: Access Transparency logs show when Google staff access data.

scenario: Which security approach keeps a whole app's software supply chain secure, from code to deployment?

options.text: Software supply chain security (e.g., Binary Authorization)
Using shared admin accounts for deployments

explanation: Binary Authorization allows only trusted images to deploy.

scenario: Which Google Cloud tools help monitor app performance and logs?
explanation: Alerts can notify teams before users notice problems.

scenario: What does site reliability engineering (SRE) focus on?

options.text: Applying software engineering to keep services reliable
Manually restarting servers when they fail

explanation: SRE uses SLIs, SLOs and error budgets.

scenario: Which term describes the target level of reliability for a service, like 99.9% availability?

options.note: A contract with consequences, not the internal target.

explanation: SLAs are contractual commitments to customers.

scenario: Which tool helps teams understand and control cloud spending?
explanation: Budgets can send alerts at spending thresholds.

scenario: Which practice organizes resources so costs can be tracked by team?
explanation: Export billing data to BigQuery for detailed analysis.

scenario: Which describes a blameless postmortem?

options.text: A review that focuses on fixing systems, not blaming people

explanation: Postmortems improve reliability through learning.

scenario: Which Google Cloud support resource offers help for issues with paid technical support?

options.note: Free peer help, not paid support.

explanation: Plans include Standard, Enhanced and Premium Support.

scenario: What's a benefit of autoscaling for operations?

options.text: Capacity matches demand without manual work
It removes the need for monitoring
It prevents all outages and failures

explanation: Autoscaling balances performance and cost.

scenario: Which describes infrastructure as code?

options.text: Defining infrastructure in files for repeatable deployments
Drawing network diagrams in a design tool

explanation: Terraform is commonly used with Google Cloud.
